subject: Service obligation calibration & monthly remedy proposal — QuantaMetrics
messages:
From: Danielle Lee <danielle@quantametrics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantametrics.com
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA asks and monthly remedy expectations

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for yesterday’s demo — QuantaMetrics is excited about Redwood’s latency profiles. Procurement asked me to send our standard SLA requests so we can see where there’s alignment ahead of legal redlines. High level:

- We need a baseline availability metric and a monthly monetary remedy schedule.
- Prefer 99.95% for mission-critical endpoints, with credits calculated as a percentage of the monthly invoice.
- We also expect p95 and p99 latency SLOs for the generation endpoint (with definitions for measurement windows).
- Scheduled maintenance windows and maintenance notice periods must be explicit; we can accept up to 2 hours/month maintenance if communicated 72 hours in advance.

I’m attaching our SOW and a simple SLA_request_form.xlsx with the items procurement wants covered. Can Redwood provide an initial counter with: uptime bands, credit percentages, a max-monthly cap, and any carveouts (maintenance, region failover, batched inference)?

We’d like a short call this week to move the draft forward — are you available Thu or Fri afternoon PT?

Thanks,
Danielle Lee
Head of Procurement
QuantaMetrics Inc

Attachments: QuantaMetrics_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf), SLA_request_form.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Lee <danielle@quantametrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 12:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks and monthly remedy expectations

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear list and the SOW. I’ve reviewed the procurement form and sketched a counterproposal for discussion below. Happy to jump on a call Thu 2pm PT.

Proposed (initial) positions from Redwood:
- Availability: Hosted API endpoints — 99.9% monthly uptime; Dedicated (reserved) pools — 99.95% monthly uptime.
- Remedy bands (monthly invoice credit):
  - 99.99–100.00%: 0%
  - 99.9–99.989%: 5% of monthly recurring charges for affected service
  - 99.0–99.899%: 15%
  - <99.0%: 30% (up to a cap)
- Cap: total credits capped at 50% of a single month’s recurring fees; credits issued as invoice credits the following billing cycle.
- Carveouts: Scheduled maintenance (as ≤2 hrs/month with 72hrs notice), force majeure, customer misconfiguration, network issues outside Redwood control.
- Latency: We can commit to p95 for small payloads (<=512 tokens) at 250ms for hosted and 150ms for dedicated; p99 is offered as a best-effort metric with alerting but not a monetary remedy in the initial pilot.
- Batched inference: due to batching behavior, these workloads will be scoped separately — we can include a batched-workload addendum with different SLOs or remove them from the availability calculation.

Open items for your input:
- Does QuantaMetrics need p99 as a monetary SLO or is alerting + runbook acceptable initially?
- Confirm whether the cap should be higher than 50% for this enterprise deal.

I’ve attached a short counter (redwood_sla_counter_v1.pdf) with the above mapped to the SOW sections. Laura — can you review the credit wording and escalation path language prior to Thu? Ben — can you confirm commercial alignment on the cap and whether we can do a pilot exception for p99 later?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_sla_counter_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00

Quick internal note — copying Laura for legal review.

- Commercial stance: I’m comfortable with the 50% monthly cap as an initial ask for a mid-market expansion; for enterprise we can consider a ramped cap tied to committed spend. Suggest pushback only if procurement insists on >75% cap.
- Maintenance: recommend we keep the 72-hr notice but propose a quarterly maintenance calendar option that reduces ad-hoc downtime.
- Escalation: propose a three-tier escalation (Support -> Customer Success -> VP of Ops) with SLA breach reporting timelines in the redline.

Laura — any legal concerns on remedy calculation wording or the carveouts above?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts

From: Danielle Lee <danielle@quantametrics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantametrics.com
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service obligation calibration & monthly remedy proposal — QuantaMetrics

Stephanie, Ben — thanks for the quick counter and internal notes. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:

- The 99.9% vs 99.95% split could work if we get stronger latency guarantees for hosted endpoints used in customer-facing flows. We remain firm on p99 latency as an operational SLO — if not monetary, it should trigger a defined remediation plan and rolling credits if regressions persist over 2 consecutive months.
- Batched inference carveout: we accept a separate addendum but need clear language that batched jobs will not dilute monthly availability for real-time endpoints.
- Cap: QM prefers a cap of 60% for the first six months of the agreement, then revert to 50% afterward. Is Redwood willing to agree to this ramp for the pilot?

Next steps: please produce a revised counter that: (1) adds a p99 operational SLO with an automatic remediation runbook trigger, (2) captures the 60% initial cap for 6 months, and (3) includes a short batched-inference addendum draft. If all looks aligned we can route to DocuSign — I’ve included a link below for an internal signature flow.

DocuSign (procurement): https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-QuantaMetrics-SLA

Happy to take the Thu 2pm PT call as well — send an invite and any pre-reads.

Regards,
Danielle Lee
Head of Procurement
QuantaMetrics Inc
